intro: Machado torched the Dodgers and shot the Padres to the top of the Wild-Card standings, and it wasn't even a conversation. Meanwhile, Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow — again — because apparently once just wasn't enough.

stories.headline: Machado Wrecks the Dodgers and Sends the Padres to the Top of the Wild-Card Pile
stories.body: Manny Machado went yard and drove in three as San Diego knocked off Los Angeles 5-1, vaulting the Padres to the top NL wild-card spot and one win away from a third straight postseason. Fernando Tatis Jr. chipped in three hits because apparently one superstar showing up wasn't enough.

stories.headline: Phillies and Astros Punch Their Tickets on the Last Possible Day
stories.body: Both Philadelphia and Houston clinched playoff spots on Game 162, with Houston edging out the Rangers after the two clubs spent the week literally tied atop the AL West at 78-79. Nothing like waiting until the absolute last second to make it interesting.

stories.headline: Blake Treinen Hurts His Shoulder Before He Even Gets Into the Game
stories.body: Dodgers reliever Blake Treinen exited with a shoulder injury sustained while warming up in the bullpen during Saturday's 4-3 win over the Giants — tough timing with the postseason around the corner. Los Angeles got the win, but that's a brutal footnote heading into October.

stories.headline: Jayden Daniels Dislocates His Elbow Again — Yes, Again
stories.body: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow for the second time since last season, ruling him out for Week 3 against Seattle. He's not on IR, so a return is technically possible, but two dislocations in under a year is not exactly a confidence booster.

stories.headline: Jaxson Dart's Rookie Year Is Over After Knee Surgery
stories.body: Giants QB Jaxson Dart is done for the regular season after suffering a knee injury against the Rams, with surgery now confirmed. New York's quarterback situation just went from a fun storyline to a full-blown problem in a hurry.

stories.headline: Nick Chubb Retiring as a Brown, the Way It Should Be
stories.body: Browns RB Nick Chubb will officially retire as a Cleveland Brown in a ceremony on Friday, the team announced. After everything his body went through, it's a genuinely nice ending to one of the more quietly beloved careers in recent NFL history.

stories.headline: U.S. Steamrolls Sunday Singles to Steal the Presidents Cup from Medinah
stories.body: The Americans won nine of 12 singles matches on Sunday to erase a three-point deficit and take the Presidents Cup at Medinah Country Club. Turns out a three-point lead with one day to play means absolutely nothing when the U.S. shows up.

stories.headline: Bridgeman Goes Scorched Earth with a 61 to Win the Biltmore Championship
stories.body: Jacob Bridgeman trailed by five shots and responded with a career-best 10-under 61, winning the inaugural Biltmore Championship Asheville for his second PGA Tour victory of the season. Nothing like opening the fall swing by making everyone else look like they were playing a different sport.

stories.headline: Fitzpatrick Laps the Field in France, Closes in on Fourth Title of 2026
stories.body: Matt Fitzpatrick led by five shots heading into the final round of the FedEx Open de France at Le Golf National and did exactly what you'd expect — he closed it out for his fourth win of the year. At some point the DP World Tour should just mail him the trophy early.

stories.headline: Florida Absolutely Demolished No. 4 Ole Miss, and It Wasn't Close
stories.body: The Gators torched Ole Miss 52-28 in one of the week's nastiest upsets, sending the Rebels tumbling out of the top four and launching Florida into the top 10. Ole Miss had just climbed to No. 4 — enjoy the view while it lasted.

stories.headline: Texas Survives Tennessee in a Nail-Biter, Stays in the Top 3
stories.body: Texas escaped Knoxville with a 20-17 win over Tennessee in the marquee matchup of the weekend, holding onto their spot in the AP top three alongside Georgia and Notre Dame. Three points is three points — a win's a win.

stories.headline: Bill Belichick at UNC Comes With a Catch, Per the Chancellor
stories.body: UNC's chancellor made it clear this week that the program's support for Bill Belichick "comes with expectations" — a fairly pointed thing to say about your own head coach in September. The Belichick-to-college experiment keeps getting more interesting by the week.

stories.headline: Messi Who? Jamal Thiaré Breaks Inter Miami Hearts in the 98th Minute
stories.body: Columbus Crew beat Inter Miami 2–1 on Saturday in front of a record 21,188 fans at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, with Jamal Thiaré's stoppage-time winner canceling out Lionel Messi's equalizer. Josef Martínez had given Miami the lead from the spot, but apparently nobody told Columbus the script.

stories.headline: Raphinha Is on Fire and Deco Has Already Forgotten Julián Álvarez's Name
stories.body: Barcelona's Raphinha has scored 14 goals in eight matches — 12 of them in La Liga — and sporting director Deco bluntly declared Álvarez "is in the past" as Raphinha slides into the centre-forward role. He's currently outscoring both Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé, which is not a sentence anyone predicted writing this season.

stories.headline: Pulisic Stays Paid: AC Milan Eye Contract Extension Through 2031
stories.body: AC Milan are reportedly planning to hand Christian Pulisic a new deal worth around €5 million per season through summer 2031, following his goal in a 3–0 dismantling of Lecce. Good week to be the USMNT's favorite son in Serie A.

stories.headline: Russell Snatches Baku Win From Verstappen by a Blink
stories.body: George Russell beat Max Verstappen by less than two tenths of a second in Azerbaijan, with Isack Hadjar rounding out the podium. Russell trims Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points — close enough to matter, not close enough to panic about yet.

stories.headline: Colapinto Wipes Out Norris, Norris Wants Him Gone
stories.body: Franco Colapinto collected a 10-second penalty for causing the safety-car restart crash that ended Lando Norris's race in Baku. Norris responded by publicly calling for Colapinto to be banned, which is about as subtle as the crash itself.

stories.headline: Ocon Out at Haas, Antonelli Says the Title Fight Isn't Over
stories.body: Haas is expected to cut Esteban Ocon loose at season's end with no renewal offer on the table. Meanwhile, Kimi Antonelli — still leading the championship by 66 points — insists the title race is 'not over,' which is technically true but a strange hill to plant a flag on.

stories.headline: Fernandez Goes Full Scorched Earth in Singapore, Wins Last 9 Games to Claim Title
stories.body: Leylah Fernandez won the WTA 500 in Singapore by winning the final nine games against Talia Gibson — which is a very Fernandez way to do it. It's her sixth career title and punches her back into the Top 30.

stories.headline: Kimberly Birrell Beats a Fellow Australian for Her First WTA Title Because of Course She Did
stories.body: Birrell took the Seoul title in an all-Australian final, cracking the Top 50 in the process and picking up her first WTA Tour singles trophy. The Czech Republic also won the Billie Jean King Cup for the 12th time, with Noskova and Muchova shutting out Ukraine 2-0 in Shenzhen.

stories.headline: Draper Out Until 2027, Alcaraz Thriving — Business as Usual on the Men's Side
stories.body: Jack Draper is sidelined until 2027, which is rough news for anyone who had him circled for the fall stretch. Meanwhile, Carlos Alcaraz beat Taylor Fritz at the Laver Cup to put Team Europe up 7-5, because Alcaraz apparently doesn't do slumps.

stories.headline: Fantilli Gets Paid: Columbus Locks Up Their Guy for $82.5M
stories.body: Adam Fantilli signed a six-year, $82.5 million extension with the Columbus Blue Jackets on Sept. 25, carrying a $13.75M cap hit that puts him among the NHL's elite earners. The standoff is over — now Columbus just has to build a winner around him.

stories.headline: Hellebuyck Watch Is Officially a Thing Now
stories.body: Connor Hellebuyck's name kept popping up in trade rumors all week, with multiple reports linking the Jets goalie to potential destinations around the league. Winnipeg hasn't moved him yet, but the noise isn't dying down.

stories.headline: Pastrnak Gets the 'C' in Boston
stories.body: David Pastrnak was named captain of the Boston Bruins on Sept. 27, filling the void left when Brad Marchand was traded back in March 2025. Safe to say the Bruins didn't have to look very far for their next leader.

stories.headline: Curry Inks $116M Extension, Not Done Bleeding the Warriors Dry Just Yet
stories.body: Stephen Curry signed a two-year, $116 million extension to stay in Golden State, because of course he did. At this point, the Warriors wouldn't know what to do with themselves if Steph was somewhere else.

stories.headline: Buddy Hield Is Basically a Moving Box at This Point
stories.body: Hield was shipped from Atlanta to Charlotte as part of a Dorian Finney-Smith deal, then almost immediately flipped again to Chicago in a separate Rob Dillingham trade — all in the same week. The man has logged more miles than a FedEx truck this offseason.

stories.headline: Bucks Under Investigation, Ballmer Suspended — The NBA's Got Drama Before a Ball Is Tipped
stories.body: Milwaukee is being investigated for possible salary-cap circumvention tied to a Gary Trent Jr. deal, while the Clippers named John Gibson interim governor after Steve Ballmer was suspended over the Kawhi Leonard situation. Training camp hasn't even started and the league already needs a spreadsheet to track the chaos.
